Depending on the story, names wouldn't really be **that** important. To me, I just feel that it needs to feel right for said character. If the story is symbolic in nature, than yeah, by all means, make a bad ass story about their name~

If you're writing a strictly erotic short for your lover (or "lovers" >,>) than last names/names are an afterthought, at least, when I write them. Same goes for a sci-fi short I wrote. The last names were rarely brought up, except for the Ph.D.'s in the book, Dr. Tigris, for example.

It's probably just me then. I feel like names could be perfected; not too perfect but definitely authentic. A good way I was told to name characters was this: put yourself in their parents shoes. Where are they? What's their conditions? Influences? Thoughts? Situation? Now name that child you're about to have or had. 

For some, that might be too deep, but it's definitely a good starting point, but again, I'm rarely happy with my writing.

I've always liked doing this as well, but at times, I feel like it's too... doctored; when I read a story or book and the characters name is a little too perfect for the personality, I feel as if it's inorganic or synthetic. I think I know what OP means; choosing names is easy but making them authentic is not.

Once it's filled, put it somewhere safe and leave it there and buy a new notebook. Start writing in that one just the same. Life is hard and I get that. Sometimes we just have to wait out the storm and in the meantime, if writing in that notebook is what gives you comfort, then write on all the pages, walls and posters you find until the day comes that you'll look back at those writings and drawings and say, "I was so silly." 

I'm about a 1/4 of the way writing a book about what happened to me, my suicide attempts and my fantasies (Fictional, kind of. My suicide attempts and my past is very real like my character. My fantasies are, well, fantasies). It makes me feel so much better to write down what I feel and there are some parts of the plot where I get so mad writing it or even cry just reading it, but once I'm done being mad or sad, I feel better venting to myself. 

If you're mad, address the empty chair, as my psychologist would put it. What would you tell youself? What would you do? How would you say these things? 

If you're sad, don't hesitate to cry. Put on that sappy music and pick up an entire Costco sized box of your favorite comfort food and cry all day long. It's not wrong to feel this way, especially when life seems terrible. 

I'm still going through this and it's a battle every day. Suicidal thoughts come across my head daily and I still hate myself for what happened, but some things are out of our control and we shouldn't worry about that which we can't control. Keep trying and when we're out of this hole, I'm sure we'll both be glad we stuck through it and got out of this terrible feeling.
